sentences.text: Brighstoneus possesses a unique nasal bulla where the nasal bone bulges upward past the nostril opening, a feature rare among iguanodontians.
The dorsal surface of this nasal bone forms an almost entirely unique "S"-shape when viewed from the side.
In this dinosaur, the maxillary process accounts for roughly 60% of the jugal bone's length, a proportion higher than in most hadrosauriforms but similar to Ouranosaurus.
The predentary bone features a bilobed, heart-shaped process on its underside, while the dorsal surface bears a series of large denticles.
Among hadrosauriforms with a system of active and replacement teeth in the same socket, Brighstoneus holds the record for the highest number of alveoli.
A 2024 estimate by Gregory S. Paul suggests Brighstoneus was approximately 6 meters long and weighed about 1 ton.
Brighstoneus is a genus of hadrosauriform dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, England, containing only one known species.
The holotype specimen MIWG 6344 was discovered in the summer of 1978 after a storm caused a collapse at Grange Chine.
Remains initially thought to be Iguanodon generated significant interest in the early 1980s, leading to further collection efforts.

Brighstoneus was identified as distinct from Mantellisaurus in 2019 by Jeremy Lockwood during his PhD research at the University of Portsmouth, and formally named in 2021 by Lockwood, David Martill, and Susannah Maidment.
The species name simmondsi honors Keith Simmonds, who assisted in the discovery of the remains.
The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that includes the skull and lower jaws.
Only one fossil occurrence of Brighstoneus has been recorded.
The original description noted that Brighstoneus was large in size but did not provide specific estimates for dimensions or body mass.
The dentary row contains 28 tooth sockets, with a potential additional socket indicated by a small pit on the right dentary.
Phylogenetic analyses in 2021 placed Brighstoneus within the clade Iguanodontia.
Most analyses suggest Brighstoneus is a basal member of Hadrosauriformes, forming a polytomy with Barilium, Hypselospinus, Iguanodon, and Mantellisaurus.
One analysis excluding specific nasal and ilium characters recovered Brighstoneus outside Hadrosauriformes as a sister species to Ouranosaurus.
A 2024 study by Lockwood et al. recovered Brighstoneus as the earliest-diverging member of Hadrosauroidea within Hadrosauriformes.
A 2025 study by Bertozzo et al. recovered Brighstoneus as the sister taxon to a clade containing Comptonatus and Brighstoneus, placing these taxa within Hadrosauroidea after the Iguanodontidae.
A 2026 study by Huang et al. using an updated matrix recovered a comparable clade for these taxa.
Brighstoneus belongs to the parent group Hadrosauriformes and is classified within the class Ornithischia.
The type species of the genus Brighstoneus is Brighstoneus simmondsi.
The holotype of Brighstoneus was found in Barremian deposits of the Wessex Formation, where the animal lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
Brighstoneus lived on a floodplain environment intersected by rivers and lakes.
Water levels in Brighstoneus's habitat varied seasonally due to high evaporation despite significant precipitation.
The environment experienced frequent extreme storms and floods that deposited dead organisms in ponds.
Frequent wildfires occurred in the habitat, which prevented the dense growth of gymnosperms.
